analysis.title: US Weekly Kickstart: Three conditions to support an S&P 500 correction bottom
key_insights: The S&P 500 is down 12% from its October 6 record high, more than the 10% median calendar-year peak-to-trough decline since 1980. The Nasdaq-100 is down 20% from its high and down 1% YTD.
After 22 S&P 500 corrections of 10% since 1980, the index returned an average of 4% over the next 3 months and rose in 17 of 22 (73%) of those episodes.
The S&P 500 forward P/E is down 25% YTD to 16x, near the historical average. The cyclically-adjusted P/E on trend earnings is down 10% YTD and sits in the 83rd percentile since 1990.

Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth exceeded 30% y/y, but investors are focused on the medium-term earnings outlook. The AI investment boom has lifted S&P 500 earnings about 25% above their 30-year trend, which creates downside risk as capex tailwinds fade.

Downside scenario: the 30-year average P/E of 17x on trend EPS of $340 implies an S&P 500 near 5,800, or roughly 13x-14x consensus 2027 EPS. Upside scenario: the P/E recovering to the 10-year average of 19x implies a new high of 8,100.

The sell-off was concentrated in the AI complex and widened this week into a broader growth shock. The GS AI basket is down 32% since October 6 and down 4% YTD. The S&P 500 ex. AI is now 6% off its high.
Cyclicals have lagged defensives by 5 pp over the past ten days, after trading in line with them for most of the past month. GS reads this as equities revising down the growth outlook.
GS recommends diversifying with select defensives and owning companies with strong buybacks.
Some investors compare the sell-off to late 2018. GS sees ongoing Fed tightening as the common element. The GS Financial Conditions Index has tightened both including and excluding equities.

GS lists three conditions that would support an equity bottom: (1) news that raises confidence in the earnings trajectory from AI investment and monetization, (2) a better macro backdrop such as a dovish Fed signal, (3) a major decline in investor positioning.

Hedge fund selling has been heavy and net leverage is at its lowest since April 2025. The Hedge Fund VIP basket (GSTHHVIP) has lagged the S&P 500 by 14 pp over six months, close to its worst relative performance in 20 years. GS says equity volatility is showing signs of severe stress.

Broad positioning is still elevated. The GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator is 0.7, above average. US equity mutual funds and ETFs took in nearly $170 billion QTD, and asset manager net equity futures length is in the 82nd percentile of the past 10 years.

Hedge funds and mutual funds are both overweight Health Care, Industrials and Financials. Both added to Consumer Discretionary and cut Communication Services in Q3. Mutual funds added to Info Tech and Energy while hedge funds cut them. Mutual funds cut Financials and Consumer Staples while hedge funds added.

Eight 'shared favorite' stocks appear in both the hedge fund VIP and mutual fund overweight baskets: APH, COF, DHR, MA, SPCX, SPOT, UNH and V. APH, DHR, SPOT and UNH are new this quarter, and BA and TMO dropped out.
A rolling portfolio of shared favorites is up 28% YTD, 15 pp ahead of the equal-weight S&P 500. Since 2013 it has returned 17% a year with a 22% standard deviation.

Fund performance is dispersed. US equity long/short hedge funds are up 5% YTD and the average large-cap mutual fund is up 5%, with 42% of funds beating benchmarks. 82% of growth funds have outperformed against 4% of value funds.

GS forecasts: S&P 500 EPS $375 in 2026, $415 in 2027 and $460 in 2028, against bottom-up consensus of $370, $429 and $500. GS targets 8,000 for YE 2026 and 8,700 at 12 months, a 21% return from the current 7,176.
The macro team's 12-month forecasts include a US 10-year yield of 4.6% (from 5.0% now), Brent at $80 (from $92) and COMEX gold at $4,540 (from $3,686).

GS top-down 2026 EPS growth by sector: Info Tech +68%, Comm Services +64%, Energy +82%, Financials +15%, Health Care 0%. GS expects 2027 growth of -18% for Comm Services, -10% for Cons Discretionary and -9% for Energy. All are forecasts.
Consensus 2026 EPS growth for selected names: NVDA +101%, MU +871%, AMD +94%, BE +453% and COIN -135%. These are consensus estimates.

tension_points.bull_case: The forward P/E has fallen 25% YTD to 16x, near the historical average. Past 10% corrections were followed by an average 4% gain over 3 months, with the index up in 73% of cases. If investors regain confidence in consensus earnings, the P/E can recover to the 10-year average and the S&P 500 can reach 8,100.
tension_points.bear_case: The cyclically-adjusted P/E on trend EPS is in the 83rd percentile since 1990. Earnings run about 25% above trend because of AI capex, so a 17x multiple on $340 of trend EPS implies about 5,800. Broad positioning is still elevated, and the sell-off has widened into a growth downgrade.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A bottom needs one of three conditions: renewed confidence in AI earnings, a dovish Fed signal, or a major drop in investor positioning. The 5,800 downside level would be in play if investors apply the 30-year average P/E to trend EPS.
